task.name: Accumulating run outcomes and deriving the signals routing consults share one module, so every new signal lands in the same file as the ingestion that feeds it
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2350
---

**Depends on #2350.** That issue establishes how a layered module's boundary is named — which
change-reasons are separated, and equally which length is benign and should be left intact. This
module is the second of the two the ADR grouped under that shape, and the charter that scoped the
structural milestone said the pattern is established once for both. Landing this first means
inventing a second pattern for the same problem, and then reconciling them. The edge is weaker than
a missing mechanism — this work is buildable today — but building it first makes #2350's answer
retroactive rather than authoritative.

## Why

ADR-0008 named this module as one of four whose size is worth reducing, and it is the only one of the
four with nothing tracking it. The other three each have their unit: two have landed, and the third
is #2350.

Read naively it looks like the modules already reduced, and it is not. At 3,494 lines it has 78
top-level functions with the largest at 189 — the seams exist at function level already, so there is
no god-function to name. What it lacks is a boundary between two change-reasons that share one file:

| change-reason | what lives there |
|---|---|
| accumulation | applying a completed run's outcome, merging it into a profile, updating stored history |
| signal derivation | the read model routing consults — per-role reliability, domain fit, review history, observed-cost tie-breaks |

These change for unrelated reasons. Adding a signal for routing to consult has nothing to do with how
a run's outcome is folded into stored history, but today both land in the same module, are reviewed
together, and claim the same file in the scheduler.

The cost is about to rise rather than stay flat. The signal side is what every future routing input
reads, and there are two such inputs already specified — a durable record of which capabilities a
model has demonstrated, and the structural-observer work that ranks modules by excess spend. Each
adds a reader. A read model that cannot be extended without touching the ingestion that feeds it
taxes every one of them.

As with #2350, some of this length is benign. A module that accumulates many small per-signal
derivations is legitimately long, and an issue judging itself on lines removed will collapse
derivations that are clearer apart. The problem is the shared ownership, not the size.

## Example

Today one module answers two unrelated questions, and a change to either claims the whole file:

```
model_profiles.py  (3,494 lines, 78 top-level functions)
├─ apply_run / _merge_* / _update_*      accumulation — how a finished run becomes stored history
└─ get_*_signal                          read model — what routing consults when choosing a model
```

The observable difference is that a story adding a routing signal and a story changing how outcomes
are accumulated stop serialising against each other, and a new signal can be exercised without
constructing a run outcome to feed it.

## Acceptance criteria

- The signals routing consults are readable from a module that does not import the accumulation
  side, so a change to how outcomes are stored cannot alter what a signal returns without that
  showing up as a change to the signal's own module.
- A signal can be exercised in a test that constructs the stored state it reads directly, without
  applying a run outcome to produce it.
- Adding a new routing signal writes no change to the accumulation side, and the reverse holds.
- Sprint and routing behaviour are unchanged: for the same stored history, every signal returns what
  it returned before the boundary was drawn.
- Length that is benign is left intact. A derivation is not merged into another to reduce the file,
  and the change is not judged on lines removed — the same rule #2350 records for its migration
  catalogue.

## Out of scope

Reducing this or any module below `max_module_lines`, and changing what any signal computes. This
issue draws the boundary; it does not tune the read model or add readers to it.

handoff.summary: Split model_profiles.py (3,494 lines, 78 top-level functions) into three modules following the #2350 audit_substrate pattern: model_profiles_storage.py owns accumulation (RunOutcome/ReviewerAttempt/RoleAttempt carriers, YAML I/O, apply_run and its _fold_*/_update_*/_zero_* helpers, backfill_from_history, update_from_run, summarize_profile_scope/reset_profile_data/record_profile_reset, and the canonical-ID migration with its _merge_* catalogue); model_profiles_read_model.py owns the signals routing consults (get_dev_signal, get_dev_success_rate, get_review_signal, get_role_reliability_signal, the two domain signals, get_observed_cost_tiebreak_signal, get_dev_complexity_stats, get_dev_score_cost_stats, plus _recency_params/_weighted_rate/_resolved_population/_matching_profile_entries/_resolve_identity); model_profiles_identity.py holds what both genuinely share (ROLES/COMPLEXITY_BANDS, recency defaults, RESOLVED_MODEL_*/ALIAS_DERIVED_KEY section keys, the identity resolution chain, _success_count/_metric_sum) so each name has exactly one binding. Neither owner imports the other — unlike audit_substrate, a profile signal needs only the stored dict, not a storage-opened connection — so the boundary is symmetric. model_profiles.py remains a documented re-export facade with 94 names in __all__. The move was done mechanically by AST slicing: every moved function/class and every module-level constant is verified AST-identical to HEAD, so no signal computes anything different and no derivation was merged into another. Runtime callers were repointed to the owning side (assignment/exploration/adaptive_iterations to the read model; bridge/engine/preflight/plan_flow/CLI to storage; canonical_id_from_identity callers to identity; reviewer_value's three lazy imports split by owner). Tests: 8 signal-only tests that already constructed profile dicts moved to a new test_model_profiles_read_model.py importing the read model directly; seam tests that build state via apply_run and then read a signal stayed in test_model_profiles.py, which keeps importing through the facade to keep it honest; new test_model_profiles_boundary.py (15 tests) pins the ownership in both directions including a fresh-interpreter check and a lazy-import scan. ADR-0008 gained the matching section documenting the second split.

story_deviations: Plan Step 1 placed summarize_profile_scope with the read model (per a plan-review suggestion). It is placed with storage instead: its only in-repo caller is reset_profile_data, and putting it in the read model would have forced storage to import the read model, weakening the boundary the ACs ask for. With it in storage, neither owner imports the other.

Plan-review suggested putting _windowed_rate and _metric_sum in the identity module as bidirectional helpers. _metric_sum is there (sibling of the demonstrably shared _success_count); _windowed_rate is not — its only callers are read-side, so it lives with the read model under the single-owner rule. The reviewer's bidirectional premise held for _normalize_band/_success_count and those are in identity as advised.

tests/test_assignment_routing_decision.py::test_block_building_does_not_re_read_profiles was edited to monkeypatch model_profiles_read_model instead of the facade. Patching a facade re-export rebinds only the facade's reference, so the test would have silently measured the real function. This is the same mechanical follow-through #2350 applied to tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py.

handoff.summary: Iteration 2 addressed all three P1 hard convention violations. (1) no_circular_imports — reviewer_value imported _fold_resolved_model from model_profiles_storage while storage lazily imports reviewer_value's folds from apply_run, closing a cycle. Fixed by moving _fold_resolved_model into model_profiles_identity, where the two section-key constants it writes already live: it is stdlib-only, and three accumulators across two modules (the dev and role folds in storage, the reviewer-value fold in reviewer_value) write that one breakdown, so its keys and its single writer now sit below every accumulator rather than inside one. Storage and reviewer_value both import it from identity; the facade re-exports it from its new owner and its docstring records the ownership. (2)+(3) test_mirrors_source — added tests/test_model_profiles_identity.py (26 tests over band normalization, canonical-ID derivation, transport classification, identity metadata, the _success_count/_metric_sum absent-vs-zero distinction, and the resolved-model breakdown's count/key-selection/taint behaviour) and tests/test_model_profiles_storage.py (the accumulation tests moved out of test_model_profiles.py, importing model_profiles_storage directly). test_model_profiles.py is left as the facade compatibility and seam file — every remaining test applies a run outcome and reads a signal back through theforge.model_profiles — which also brought it back under max_test_file_lines, a pre-existing violation. test_model_profiles_boundary.py gained TestNoCycleWithReviewerValue (4 tests) so the cycle cannot silently return: it scans reviewer_value's whole source including lazy imports, asserts one binding for _fold_resolved_model across identity/storage/facade, and asserts identity reaches no accumulator while still permitting its long-standing lazy hop to config.models. Verified: net-new hard convention violations against main are 0; full suite 8,641 passed with the same 17 pre-existing process-supervision failures; and the AST comparison against main:src/theforge/model_profiles.py still reports zero missing, zero changed and zero extra functions/classes, so _fold_resolved_model changed files without a character changing.

plan_review.findings:
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3's consumer list omits two src modules that reference signal names: src/theforge/domains.py and src/theforge/config/types.py. The facade keeps them working, so nothing breaks, but they are read-side callers left pointing at the compatibility shim.
  Suggestion: Either add domains.py and config/types.py to the Step 3 repoint list, or state explicitly that non-routing-critical callers intentionally stay on the facade.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
